publicComments.name: Esther Chan
publicComments.summary: As a parent at Orion Alternative, she expressed concern about reading specialist cuts and urged the board to find creative, sustainable long-term plans to support students.

publicComments.name: Tom Gerke
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about proposed music program cuts, arguing that arts education stimulates brain development and that the use of Prop 28 funds for budget shortfalls represents poor planning.

publicComments.name: Hannah Ma
publicComments.summary: Asked about alternatives to staffing cuts, expressed concerns about the distribution of cuts across schools, and urged the board to think creatively about revenue generation.

publicComments.name: Lauren Abrams
publicComments.summary: As the mental health counselor at Taft, she described the high-trauma demographics of Taft students and urged the board to reconsider reducing her position to 0.5 FTE.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent, she expressed appreciation for the district and proposed that a significantly higher parcel tax—comparable to neighboring districts—could close the budget gap.

publicComments.name: Marianne Nakla
publicComments.summary: As the mental health liaison at Henry Ford, she urged the board to reconsider cutting mental health liaison positions at Taft, Henry Ford, Orion, and Adelante Selby.

publicComments.name: Lizbeth Estrada
publicComments.summary: A Hoover parent speaking in Spanish (with interpretation), she expressed deep gratitude to Dr. Baker for his focus on equity and his positive impact on the Hoover school community.

publicComments.name: Saoirse Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A 4th grader at Orion, she said she loves her school and teachers, expressed confidence the district can adapt, and hoped for a larger parcel tax so all kids can have what they need.

publicComments.name: Sue Jorgensen
publicComments.summary: A Taft librarian, she criticized the lack of communication from the district about the layoffs and the inadvertent disclosure of retiring colleagues, and stated she is not yet convinced to support a parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Anne Barloffa
publicComments.summary: A 32-year district employee, she advocated for enshrining a 25-to-1 class size ratio for K-2 classrooms into the contract, warning that larger class sizes cause vulnerable students to fall through the cracks.

publicComments.name: Sherry Tsukiyama
publicComments.summary: A 1st grade teacher at Roosevelt, she shared personal experience of how the 25-student cap has dramatically improved her ability to meet students' needs and urged the board to enshrine it in the contract.

publicComments.name: Jessica McClain
publicComments.summary: An education specialist, she raised concerns about alarmingly high special education caseload numbers, arguing that reduced caseloads—achieved by opening additional classrooms—would better serve the most vulnerable students.

publicComments.name: Allison Sudol
publicComments.summary: A special education teacher at Roosevelt, she described how rising caseloads since 2019 have led to unsafe behaviors and dysregulation, and proposed opening additional extensive support needs classrooms to bring caseloads down to safe levels.

publicComments.name: Aaron Washburn
publicComments.summary: A music teacher and CTA president, he described the wide-ranging academic, social-emotional, and community benefits of well-funded elementary music programs and urged administrators and parents to prioritize them.

publicComments.name: Diane Gutierrez
publicComments.summary: A school counselor at Orion, she shared a story of a dysregulated student to illustrate the vital importance of having a consistent, accessible mental health counselor at every school site.

publicComments.name: Lily Milton
publicComments.summary: An Orion/Kennedy parent and RCEF board member, she urged the board to reject the resolution, seek authentic educator input, take an equitable approach to any cuts, and work to rebuild community trust before pursuing a parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Dave Freilich
publicComments.summary: He acknowledged the board's difficult position but called it unconscionable to cut librarians, mental health professionals, and STEM teachers in such a high-cost area, and echoed calls for creative solutions before cutting positions.

items.title: Adoption of Resolution No. 8, Reduction of Certain Classified Services for Fiscal Year 2023-2024

publicComments.name: Salvador Gomez Nava
publicComments.summary: A Taft parent speaking in Spanish (with interpretation), he stressed the critical importance of school counseling for traumatized students, including his 7-year-old daughter, warning that without support, children could face severe consequences.

publicComments.name: Anna Solorio
publicComments.summary: As president of CSEA Chapter 5, she formally opposed the layoff of any classified employees and requested the board not approve the classified layoff resolution.

publicComments.name: Connie Hamilton
publicComments.summary: A librarian at Clifford with 11 years of experience, she questioned the logic of laying off low-paid LMA librarians while hiring new higher-paid LMTAs, described her deep relationships with students, and called the situation insulting and devastating.

publicComments.name: Beverly Aguilar
publicComments.summary: The librarian at Garfield, she explained that the LMAs' positions are being eliminated despite doing the same work as LMTAs, noted their pending reclassification request had been recommended for approval, and asked the board not to eliminate their positions given their combined 30 years of experience.

items.title: Adoption of Resolution No. 9, Release and Reassignment of Certificated Administrators
Approval of Release of Temporary Teachers
Approval of Agreement between the Redwood City School District and TeamCivX and Godbe Research to conduct a Parcel Tax Measure Feasibility Study

publicComments.name: Chris Rabell
publicComments.summary: He urged the board to be transparent with the community about whether a new bond is also planned alongside the parcel tax, citing concerns about the cumulative tax burden on residents given many other pending taxes and bond measures.
